en.title: Maximum Sum of a Fixed-Length Window with Distinct Elements
en.description:
Choose a contiguous window of length exactly k whose elements are pairwise distinct, maximizing the sum of its elements. If there is no valid window, output −1.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; supplements to missing source bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n k, and the second line contains n integers; when n=0, the second line may be empty. The source gives no size or value range; this site adds 0≤n≤200000, 1≤k≤200000, and −10^9≤a[i]≤10^9; k may be greater than n, and negative numbers are not excluded.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 15; -5; -1. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Maintain the sum and the value frequencies of a sliding window of length k; when the frequency table has size k, the elements are distinct. Use a separate not-found flag when updating the maximum.
